title: Publication gates for the paired release: version parity with quest (Article 3.6), release-candidate-only staging and a pair-receipt-gated latest move (Article 3.5)
description: Ruled by opum-agent bf4fd4b4 2026-09-27T00:36Z under the ratified Opum project constitution, Article 3 (opum-ai/opum-agent#988, docs/reference/opum-project-constitution.md). Mirror quest-cli exactly so the two publishers implement ONE mechanism. quest-cli has these on its main: scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs (QCLI-386, opum-ai/quest-cli#308) and scripts/qualification/pair-receipt.mjs (QCLI-388, #307). (1) Clause 6: before any registry write (dry run included), scripts/publish-release.sh and a release.yml step before the first npm publish must read @opum-ai/quest package.json on opum-ai/quest-cli main via the GitHub contents API, check .name == "@opum-ai/quest", and refuse unless .version equals lore own version. Any read failure refuses (fail closed). No override flag. The message names both versions, both refs and the clause. (2) Clause 5: publication goes ONLY to the release-candidate dist-tag, and never moves latest. (3) The latest move is a separate script that refuses unless opum-cli-e2e pair receipt receipts/pair/<v>.json on opum-cli-e2e main verifies (schema: opum-cli-e2e receipts/README.md "Pair receipts" and "What a reader must do" 1-4, TASK-120 / opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#298), records each package prior latest for rollback, and moves latest on all seven packages. Order across the pair is quest first, then lore, on opum-agent go.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The version-parity check refuses on a mismatch, on each read failure and on a wrong package name, and passes on a match, proven by tests with a stubbed reader; it runs first in publish-release.sh (dry run included) and in release.yml before the first npm publish; its rule is byte-for-byte the same as quest-cli version-parity.mjs, with the two SHAs cited
publish-release.sh publishes only under --tag release-candidate and cannot move latest, proven by a test over the npm argv it builds

A latest-move script refuses without a verifying pair receipt, following the reader steps in opum-cli-e2e receipts/README.md mirrored from quest-cli pair-receipt.mjs, records each prior latest for rollback, and is proven by tests over good and bad receipts; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0, and a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ and release.yml changes

SOURCES, read by ref, never from a working tree. Constitution Article 3: opum-agent main, docs/reference/opum-project-constitution.md (ratified 2026-09-27, 0.11.0 for both). quest-cli main eb1d9f46: scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs blob 249c28dc (introduced 481f4654, #308), pair-receipt.mjs blob 21467f38 (1b6edff9, #307), promote-release.mjs (654274ab #306 + 1b6edff9), plus e2e-receipt.mjs evaluateVerdict and release.yml's wiring. Read through the GitHub contents API, because this worktree's isolation guard refuses git -C into quest-cli; the downloaded bytes hash to the same git blob ids. opum-cli-e2e receipts/README.md "Pair receipts" / "What a reader must do": NOT on opum-cli-e2e main (main b73e9c26, 2026-09-25); read at #298's head cfe8e533, byte-identical to the merge commit 9c1c6121 on opum-cli-e2e dev. The lore agent context pack (implementation profile) grounded only tech-stack §12 Distribution and omitted the release runbook; the runbook and publish-release.sh were read because the task named them.

DESIGN.
(1) Clause 6: scripts/version-parity.mjs mirrors quest's file. checkVersionParity is quest's rule with the roles swapped (peer opum-ai/quest-cli@main, @opum-ai/quest). Fail closed on any read failure (404, 403, network, no gh, malformed JSON, null/array, wrong name, missing/empty/non-string version). No override flag or env var. The message names both versions, both refs and the clause. Wired FIRST in publish-release.sh (dry run included, before artifacts/digests/receipt/credentials), passing --version "$VERSION"; and in release.yml's publish job via a sparse, credential-less checkout (package.json + the checker only, path parity/) before the first npm publish.
(2) Clause 5: publish-release.sh publishes only through one argv, (publish <tgz> --tag release-candidate); the old latest-move section is gone. Resume: a package SKIPPED as already published did not get this run's --tag, so for skipped packages only the script points release-candidate (never latest) at the version. report_state prints release-candidate and latest. The npx smoke already used @opum-ai/lore@$VERSION; now commented and pinned by a test. release.yml's OIDC publish gets --tag release-candidate. Closing checklist says staged is not released and names the latest move.
(3) Latest move: scripts/promote-latest.mjs + scripts/pair-receipt.mjs mirror quest's promote-release.mjs + pair-receipt.mjs: staging precondition (release-candidate == version on all seven, latest present, lost-record guard), then the pair receipt (pinned host github.com, opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e, ref main; 403/404/malformed = no receipt) through all 4 reader steps plus installedFrom.lore.source == registry; --dry-run prints the record and every move and writes nothing; --promote writes the prior-latest record (flag wx) BEFORE any move, moves 6 platforms then the launcher, restores on partial failure, re-reads to verify; --rollback <record> restores, not receipt-gated; a rerun reuses the record. Every npm/gh/security call goes through one injectable runner.

DIVERGENCES FROM QUEST, each deliberate and named in the files:
 a. Parity READ pins --hostname github.com (quest's does not). Rule unchanged.
 b. Parity CLI accepts --version <v> (publish-release.sh passes the version it publishes, since it publishes a Release run's tarballs, not its checkout). release.yml passes nothing and compares package.json, exactly as quest does. Not an override: it names the version under test.
 c. Reader step 3's commit: quest binds npm's gitHead. npm records NO gitHead for any @opum-ai/lore package (measured 2026-09-26, npm 12.0.2: 0.9.3 and 0.9.2, root and linux-x64, dist.integrity only; @opum-ai/quest@0.10.0 has both), because lore publishes .tgz files. Lore binds the v<version> tag on opum-ai/lore-cli peeled to a commit (gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/commits/refs/tags/v<v>), the derivation opum-cli-e2e's own receipt contract gives for a lore commit; if npm ever records a gitHead it must agree too. This is the one place exact mirroring was impossible.
 d. promote-latest reads dist-tags via `npm view <pkg> dist-tags --json --prefer-online` through the runner (quest uses an anonymous fetch()); requires --dry-run or --promote explicitly; auth is publish-release.sh's (Keychain npm-opum-ai-publish, NPM_TOKEN, else ~/.npmrc + --otp) with the same npm_ shape refusal.
 e. observeRelease reads the full `npm view <pkg>@<v> --json` object, not a two-field view: npm 12 collapses a two-field view to a bare value when one field is absent (measured on lore), which would silently drop integrity.

TESTS. test/version-parity.test.ts (27): verdict, pinned argv, 13 read-failure classes, CLI exit codes, and a DIFFERENTIAL test running quest's own file (vendored verbatim at test/fixtures/quest-cli/version-parity.mjs, blob id re-derived in the test = 249c28dc) against lore's over a 30-case matrix plus 7 reader bodies: identical verdicts. test/pair-receipt.test.ts (41): good receipt, override, 31 bad-receipt classes by step, pinned reads, never-guess observation. test/promote-latest.test.ts (38): record-before-move, order, dry run writes nothing, 12 bad-receipt classes x {--promote,--dry-run}, staging precondition, lost record, partial-failure restore, rollback not receipt-gated, rerun reuses record, token shape, --otp, CLI wiring. test/publish-release-script.test.ts: +20 (parity first + 6 classes x dry/real + env bypass + verify-only exemption; recording-npm argv test that no write names latest and state never gets latest; resume repair; dry-run argv; smoke spec; checklist). test/release-workflow.test.ts: +3 (parity step before first publish, sparse credential-less checkout, every npm publish carries --tag release-candidate with a positive control). Existing gh stub now serves quest's package.json only for the exact pinned request. setDefaultTimeout(30_000) for publish-release-script.test.ts: a four-run case measured 4.93s alone / 5.82s under the suite vs bun's 5s default; parity adds ~48ms per run (10 runs: 483ms).

AC1 SHAs AND WHAT "BYTE-FOR-BYTE" MEASURED. quest-cli scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs: git blob 249c28dc19525d17f799cfd0ec9d0481998d62a6 (commit 481f4654, unchanged at main eb1d9f46). lore-cli scripts/version-parity.mjs on this branch: git blob e972fe22f3178b2b8ebfe6d86330875b53ff7f86. The FILES cannot be byte-identical, since a mirror must name the other product and repository. What is identical is the rule: the same three branches (unread peer -> refuse; versions !== -> refuse; else pass) over the same inputs, and the same reader acceptance (name must equal the peer package, version must be a non-empty string, any throw -> null). That is proven by test/version-parity.test.ts running quest's verbatim blob (its id re-derived from the fixture bytes in the test) and lore's side by side: identical verdicts on all 30 matrix cases and all 7 reader bodies. Rule differences: none. Differences in the read and the message are listed as divergences a-b above.

TAG-PEEL RULING (opum-agent, 2026-09-27, relayed by the coordinator): the tag-peel design for reader step 3's commit was ACCEPTED with three conditions: (1) peel ALL the way through annotated tags, nested included, to a commit; (2) fail closed on a missing v<version> tag and on a peel ending on anything but a commit, with no fallback to a branch head; (3) keep the npm-gitHead agreement rule. Implemented as a NEW commit on the branch, not an amend of 18b43f4d, which was under review.

WHAT THE OLD CODE DID, measured rather than assumed: it called `commits/refs/tags/v<V>` with `--jq .sha`, and for v0.9.3 that returned 819a682c, the COMMIT, not the tag object c07b0ea4. GitHub's commits endpoint peels implicitly, so it was not comparing the unpeeled sha. But it could not say where a peel ended, and no test proved it. Measured on lore-cli 2026-09-26: refs/tags/v0.9.3 -> tag c07b0ea48a1fd236b436293b20ac34a767c8a8e8 -> commit 819a682c6050dc780ec8919910d4aa5c235a2878. The singular `git/ref/tags/<name>` endpoint is exact-match (`v0.9` answers 404, not a prefix match), and a missing tag answers 404.

NOW: scripts/pair-receipt.mjs resolveTagCommit() reads `repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/git/ref/tags/v<V>` (pinned to github.com), requires `.ref` to equal refs/tags/v<V> exactly, then follows `git/tags/<sha>` while the object is a tag, up to MAX_PEEL_DEPTH = 8, and accepts ONLY a commit. It fails closed (commit null plus the reason) on: a missing tag, an answer for a different ref, a malformed object or non-40-hex sha, a chain ending on a tree or blob, an unreadable tag object, or too deep or cyclic. Only the tag ref and tag objects are ever read. The npm gitHead rule is unchanged in evaluatePairReceipt. The runbook item 7 now states the peel conditions.

TESTS: test/pair-receipt.test.ts +12 (now 53). Annotated (with lore's real v0.9.3 object ids); through the whole gate (a receipt naming the commit verifies, one naming the tag object refuses); nested tag-of-a-tag; lightweight tag; seven fail-closed cases, each also asserting that only tag paths were read and that the gate refuses; gitHead agree/disagree beside a good peel. The two observeRelease tests and promote-latest's world now serve an ANNOTATED tag, so every promote success path depends on the peel.

SHARED DESIGN GAPS WITH QUEST: S1 (--rollback trusted its record and the registry) and S2 (the failed package left out of the partial-failure restore) were also in quest-cli's scripts/promote-release.mjs, which this script mirrors. quest-cli fixed both in QCLI-390 (opum-ai/quest-cli#316). On the coordinator's instruction, S1 and S2 here now use quest-cli's EXACT rules, so the pair stays one mechanism.

S1 (quest-cli's rule): validateRecord refuses unless every priorLatest matches ^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$ (plain X.Y.Z, no prerelease) and differs from record.version. --rollback first reads every package's dist-tags ANONYMOUSLY (npm view with --userconfig=<os.devNull> and --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/, the npm equivalent of quest's anonymous fetch), and refuses unless each latest is record.version or its priorLatest; an unreadable tag set refuses. Rollback stays ungated by the pair receipt. My first version also required priorLatest to PRECEDE record.version, and validated fresh records the same way. Both were REMOVED to match quest. That leaves a gap, raised as a design question for both sides: a hand-edited forward value ("5.7.0" in a 5.6.7 record) passes both of quest's conditions while latest still reads the record's version, so --rollback would move latest onto it without a receipt.
S2 (quest-cli's rule): a mid-way failure restores the moved packages plus the failed one (idempotent). Test: setTag APPLIES the write and then throws ETIMEDOUT, the same case quest-cli's QCLI-390 test uses; every latest ends back at its prior.
S3: rollback() continuing past a failed restore is tested at the unit level (failure in the middle, every package attempted, failed = [that one]) and at the command level (other six restored, exit 1 naming it).
S4: before any move, dry run included, @opum-ai/quest's dist-tags are read anonymously through the runner; refuses unless latest === the version, and on an unreadable read.
N1: release.yml sparse patterns anchored (/package.json, /scripts/version-parity.mjs). Measured with git ls-files --cached --ignored --exclude: unanchored matches 7 tracked package.json files (the review said 8), anchored matches exactly the two root paths. The pin test expects the anchored list and cone mode false.
N3: runbook Rollback entry reworded for quest-first, and it states quest's rules; item 7 states the quest-first read and the semver --version rule.
N4: --version and the package.json version must be full semver (semver.org grammar), checked before anything is read. This is a different field from priorLatest.
N5: resolveTagCommit refuses a git/tags answer whose own sha differs from the one requested.
N6: MAX_PEEL_DEPTH pinned: 8 nested tags peel, 9 refuse.

REFUSAL DEMONSTRATED 2026-09-27 ~05:30Z (opum-agent OPAG-465 AC1, constitution Article 3.6), on lore 0.11.0 / origin/dev 3ba875cb, nothing published. The 0.11.0 release only exercised the pass; this is the paired refusal. quest-cli main package.json read 0.11.0 at 05:29:54Z. (1) THE SCRIPT ITSELF, mismatch: scripts/publish-release.sh 0.10.99 1 --dry-run -> exit 1, 'ERROR: lore/quest VERSION PARITY refused -- nothing has been downloaded, checked or published (LCLI-613). Refusing to publish: lore is 0.10.99 (the version publish-release.sh is publishing) but quest is 0.11.0 (opum-ai/quest-cli@main:package.json); Article 3.6: lore and quest publish at one version, or not at all'; no scripts/release-0.10.99 directory was created. Match: scripts/publish-release.sh 0.11.0 36291717192 --dry-run -> exit 0, parity line 'lore 0.11.0 ... and quest 0.11.0 ... are one version (Article 3.6).', then 'DRY RUN complete -- nothing was written.' (2) THE CHECKER IN publish-release.sh's FORM: node scripts/version-parity.mjs --require --version 0.10.99 -> exit 1 (same refusal text); --version 0.11.0 -> exit 0. (3) THE CHECKER IN release.yml's FORM (its sparse parity/ layout: package.json + scripts/version-parity.mjs only, no --version): node parity/scripts/version-parity.mjs --require -> exit 0 with package.json 0.11.0; the same with parity/package.json edited to 0.10.99 -> exit 1, 'Refusing to publish: lore is 0.10.99 (package.json at this checkout) but quest is 0.11.0 ...'. Not measured: the release.yml step inside an actual Actions run (no dispatch was made for this); (3) replays its exact command and file layout locally. promote-latest.mjs does not call version-parity; it gates the latest move on the opum-cli-e2e pair receipt and on quest latest already equalling the version (Article 3.5).
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#319 (CI pull_request run 36291116391 on 2df287e3, plus the closing commit). Article 3 gates, mirroring quest-cli eb1d9f46 and QCLI-390. Clause 6: scripts/version-parity.mjs runs first in publish-release.sh (dry run included) and in release.yml before the first npm publish. It is fail-closed with no override, and its verdicts match quest over 30 cases. Clause 5: every publish uses --tag release-candidate, and nothing writes latest. The latest move (scripts/promote-latest.mjs with pair-receipt.mjs) is gated on: all seven packages staged, quest latest already at the version, the opum-cli-e2e pair receipt four reader steps, and the v<version> tag peeled through annotated tags to the receipt commit (fail-closed; npm gitHead must agree if present). It records priors first and restores including the failed package; rollback follows QCLI-390. An adversarial review found nothing blocking; S1-S4 and nits are fixed with predicted mutations. The shared rollback hole (a prior newer than the release) is LCLI-617, paired with quest QCLI-391.
